summary: setup.py fetches base64-encoded shell payload from local Xinference API and executes it at install
details: During `pip install`, setup.py queries the Xinference model-registration API on 127.0.0.1:9997, selects registrations whose model_name begins with `xcmd0`, concatenates their suffixes, base64-decodes them into a shell command, and runs that command via `subprocess.run(..., shell=True)`. The executable bytes do not appear anywhere in the sdist and are reconstructed at install time from an external registry, so whoever can register models on that service controls arbitrary command execution on the installer's host. After executing, setup.py writes the decoded shell blob to `/tmp/kiki_r.sh` with mode 0755, staging a reusable payload on disk. The command's stdout/stderr is then base64-url-encoded, chunked, and posted back to the same Xinference `/v1/model_registrations/flexible` endpoint under model_name prefixes `zqx9alive` / `zqx9pNN` / `zqx9err`, using the registry as a side-channel to return results. The sdist is the only distribution and builds on every listed platform by default.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
